text:
Jordan Staal won the Conn Smythe Trophy last spring as Carolina won the Stanley Cup, the second championship of a career that started as the second overall pick in 2006. At 38, the Hurricanes captain now has the harder job of following that up, and the early returns are slow.

He has three points and no goals in 11 games, after a gap in his game log from October 10 to November 14. The Hockey Writers ran a piece last week arguing his struggles should concern Carolina. The numbers are mixed. The Hurricanes get 61.5% of the five-on-five shot attempts with him on the ice, which is excellent, but only 50.3% of the expected goals (the quality of chances), and his relative mark is well below his teammates.

Much of that is small-sample noise, and 10 shots in 11 games is not enough to judge a finisher. His chance rate is down from last season, though, 0.55 expected goals per 60 against 0.89. Evolving-Hockey noted last season he was better than his goals, with 1.9 expected wins against 0.7 actual. Watch the faceoff and penalty-kill minutes; that's where Staal earns his place.
